slides.title: The work that gets rejected

bullets.text: A banker spends 2-4 weeks after a conference sector-classifying hundreds of companies — or needs clean diligence the same day, because the targets fly out in 48 hours.
Even when AI does that analysis well (~58/100 on the tasks), 0% of the best model's work is client-ready. Built with 502 bankers; only ~16% was even a useful starting point.
The misses aren't IQ — they're diligence: invented numbers, dead formulas, broken audit trails. I saw exactly this leading LLMSuite adoption at JPMorgan.

slides.notes: Know your audience: rich, but a 10-year-old gets it. Lead with the visceral weeks-of-work story, then the 0% gut-punch, then the diagnosis the founder personally earned. The ~16% hedge makes the 0% MORE credible, not less.

slides.title: NodeRoom: the finance war room

bullets.text: You're right that AI will do junior-banker work. The unsolved part isn't intelligence — it's making the output sendable.
A live finance war room — spreadsheet, deck, notebook, chat — each run by a dedicated, harnessed agent. Ask in plain language; it writes evidence-bearing cells, each tied to the exact source line.
Every number tied to its exact source — cell, page, line — so the work is auditable. Designed to be accepted on the first pass.
The moat compounds as models improve: the source-tied audit trail and banker-style handoff are workflow + data lock-in, not a capability gap. Labs, Copilot, and CRMs won't build it.

slides.notes: Sell the solution by telling them THEY are right. The last bullet pre-empts the #1 VC objection ('won't frontier models just get good enough?') by reframing the moat as compounding lock-in, not a closing capability gap.

slides.title: A market we already have ground truth in

stat.label: Generative AI in financial services by 2030, growing ~39%/yr (Grand View Research). We enter where it's already real: startup & middle-market banking diligence and prospecting.

slides.notes: Add CAGR as the magical number. Wedge-first framing in the label so it doesn't read as a lazy 1%-of-a-huge-market play. Cross-firm CAGRs span 30.7%-39.1%; using Grand View's 39.1% headline with the source.

slides.title: Proof of execution — over time

bullets.text: Shipped cited-sources: hand it a claim and a PDF, it boxes the exact source line — or refuses if the quote isn't there. The thesis, as an installable skill.
Shipped the PowerPoint honesty skill that built this very deck — every claim sourced or flagged, no invented numbers.

Built our own BankerToolBench-faithful eval harness — Docker sandbox, the in-benchmark financial tools (SEC EDGAR/VDR), Gandalf verifier — running end-to-end on a scaffold smoke. No client-ready benchmark score yet; the real task runs are the next milestone.
Live in production: the harness pulls the right skill on demand (e.g. cited-sources) — how cheaper models get to client-ready.
bullets.source: shipped to production — skill RAG release (commit 66010a87)

slides.notes: Momentum = shipping velocity + a working loop, not vanity metrics. HONESTY (P0 fix): the BTB line claims ONLY what the smoke backs — no 'official', no score, no 'hill-climbs us toward client-ready'. The repo's readiness gate marks official BTB blocked; this wording survives that audit.

slides.title: Our harness, traced — honest

bullets.text: We ran a real BankerToolBench task — Disney acquiring Warner Bros Discovery, a full accretion/dilution model — through our harness on a frontier model (gpt-5.4 via Inference.ai), fully traced.
bullets.source: scripts/inference-nodetrace — real run: 3 model calls, 16k tokens

bullets.text: It reasons through all 13 components — but client-ready (Gandalf) on this exact task was ~0% (a held-out run scored 0.0078). The model's own check admits: formatting, Shift+F2 citations, sensitivity table — MISSING.
Reasoned vs. client-ready — that gap is exactly what we measure, with the trace as the proof.

slides.notes: The 'our harness, traced, honest' proof slide. Show the walkthrough GIF (scripts/inference-nodetrace/out-btb/walkthrough.gif) on this beat.

slides.title: How we make money

bullets.text: Land with seats for diligence and prospecting teams; expand to usage on agent runs as work moves into the room.
Margin lever: our harness makes cheaper open models client-ready — DeepSeek V4 Pro near $0.44 / $0.87 per million tokens, a fraction of frontier pricing.
Pricing not set yet — land design-partner pilots first, then price on proven acceptance.

slides.notes: One defended revenue line (seats -> usage) + the differentiated cheap-model margin lever. Cut the skills-marketplace second line on purpose (scope gravity at seed). Pricing stays flagged, not invented.

slides.title: Why this team

bullets.text: Solo founder today — led LLMSuite adoption at JPMorgan; banking, data engineering, and agentic AI in one person.
War-room design informed by an SVB-originated AI-notebook startup and the Meta PQX QA team.
I've done the diligence and prospecting work we're automating — that's the ground truth.
No co-founders or advisors yet — finding the right banking design-partner and field advisors is part of the ask.

slides.notes: 'Can THEY pull it off?' Yes on domain ground truth; 'battle-tested' downgraded to 'informed by' (honesty); known-unknowns reframed as first hires with a recruiting plan. Solo-founder gaps owned, not hidden.

slides.title: The ask

bullets.text: See the proof yourself: install cited-sources, give it a claim and a PDF, and watch it box the source — or refuse.
Intros to banking design partners — MDs and analysts who'll pressure-test the room on live deals.
Proof-first — not raising on a number yet: design partners and banker acceptance first, then raise against a real eval delta (client-ready off 0%).

slides.notes: Close lands on action (the live demo CTA leads), not a blank. The raise is still flagged needs_review but now tied to use-of-funds + the eval-delta milestone that directly answers the moat objection. Fill the number before presenting.
